text:
marta: Heads-up — bringing up borealis-70k-int3 for long-context tests and hit something odd. Repro script below shows coherent output until ~41k tokens, then sudden hallucination + KV mismatch. Seems like RoPE wrap/phase drift but could be quantization interaction.

marta: repro (local mimic):
```bash
# run on dev-serving w/ longctx profile
./run_eval.sh --model borealis-70k-int3 --quant int3 --context 65536 --prompt-file tests/long_64k_prompt.txt --out tmp/out.json
```
logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-12 14:12:31] step=40123 generate token=\"the\" prob=0.12
[2026-03-12 14:12:31] step=41023 kv_index=41023 fingerprint=0x1a2b
[2026-03-12 14:12:31] step=41024 generate token=\"<UNK_HALL>\" prob=0.87
[2026-03-12 14:12:31] step=41024 kv_index=41024 fingerprint=0x3c4d  # <-- unexpected change
```

kai: thanks. two quick q's: 1) does the float16 baseline hit the same token offset? 2) do you see deterministic repro across restarts and seeds?

marta: float16 baseline (borealis-70k-fp16) runs cleanly to 64k, no hallucination. Repro is deterministic on same seed across restarts.

jules: sounds like a RoPE phase wrap combined with quantized weight interpolation causing KV mismatch at rollover point. Can you dump the KV keys right before and after 41023? use tools/kv-inspect --dump-keys --idx 41020:41030

marta: ran kv-inspect. snippet: 
```
IDX 41021 key=0x9f8a... len=256 phase=0x7fff
IDX 41022 key=0xa0b3... len=256 phase=0x7fff
IDX 41023 key=0x1a2b... len=256 phase=0x7fff
IDX 41024 key=0x3c4d... len=256 phase=0x8000  # phase wrap at this index
```
So phase flips from 0x7fff -> 0x8000 exactly at 41024.

rohan: interesting — that exact phase flip is classic RoPE wrap. Two possible culprits: kernel that computes rotary exponents under int3 quant math, or index clipping when context > model-config.max_pos. Did you run with the updated rotary-scaling patch from last week?

marta: patch was on. I toggled rotary-scaling=off and reran: same flip but hallucination magnitude reduced.

jules: hmm — reduced magnitude implies quantization amplifies phase discontinuity. Can you run an int8 build and an int4-hybrid to see trend? Also check kv-compact stride, sometimes compaction algorithm mod interacts with wrap index math.

eval-bot: automated comparison result (longctx-holdout-64k):
- borealis-70k-fp16 : baseline perplexity (0-40k) 8.3, (40k-64k) 8.5
- borealis-70k-int8 : baseline perplexity (0-40k) 8.5, (40k-64k) 9.0
- borealis-70k-int3 : baseline perplexity (0-40k) 8.7, (40k-64k) 10.2  <-- sharp regression after ~41k
(artifact: >+18% relative perf delta for int3 in tail window)

rohan: that delta nails quantization as amplifier. Proposed triage steps: 1) bisect commit range for quant kernel (last 3 commits touching rotary kernel), 2) run mini reproducer with a short synthetic prompt that triggers wrap at low index (so we don't need full 64k), 3) add kv key fingerprint asserts in regression harness.

marta: I already made a short repro that triggers at 4k by using a repeated-prefix prompt (so wrap/phase happens earlier). gist: tests/repro_short_wrap.py — runs in <30s and reproduces key fingerprint swap.

kai: great work. please open an issue with: repro script link, kv dump, eval-bot results, and assign to eng-ml/roto-quant. Add the mini-repro as a failing test in tests/regressions/longwrap.

marta: done — created bug 4267 and PR #1328 to add the short repro + kv-fingerprint assert. in PR description I called out suspected kernel commit range.

kai: assigned to marta, tagging jules and rohan for visibility. thanks — let's also add a note in onboarding checklist: smoke longctx quant tests for RoPE-phase wrap when adding new quant profiles. :+1:
